## Where to find nature on a journey through Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay

**Do not expect identical wildlife-watching activities in all three countries on these itineraries.** In [Brazil](/brazil/) and [Argentina](/argentina/), some tours visit the forests around Iguazu Falls. Others continue farther south to Argentine and Chilean Patagonia. [Uruguay](/uruguay/), meanwhile, mainly offers city experiences, the Río de la Plata and the Atlantic coast on the featured routes.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} covering these three main countries and wildlife watching. The current option is a [32-day itinerary across eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) with excursions on Ecuador's Galápagos Islands: the highlands of Santa Cruz and one of two alternative sea days, North Seymour with Bachas or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. The option is confirmed after booking; encounters with particular animals are not guaranteed. The three countries in this filter **therefore do not constitute a separate uninterrupted three-country journey**. For all formats featuring this combination, see the [Argentina + Brazil + Uruguay catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_uruguay/). For nature in particular, examine the itinerary day by day.

## Iguazu Falls: the principal nature experience spanning two countries

Broad panoramas of the waterfalls open up from [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) on the Brazilian side. On the [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) side, walks follow another network of trails and viewpoints. Together, the national parks protect areas of Atlantic Forest with rich vegetation and many species of birds and animals.

It is worth distinguishing **visiting a nature park** from **a specialist trip to observe wildlife**. The forests around Iguazu provide habitat for tapirs, monkeys, large cats and other animals, but a standard waterfall excursion does not guarantee encounters with rare species. In many itineraries, the waterfalls themselves, the vegetation, the paths and the panoramas are the main attractions.

For comparison, consider the landscape-focused [nature selection for these countries](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_uruguay/interests/nature/). On the [13-day tour through Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/), the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the waterfalls are scheduled on consecutive days. After Rio and Iguazu, the itinerary moves on to Buenos Aires and Uruguay. This suits travellers seeking a major natural attraction without continuing all the way to the glaciers. The tour focuses on landscapes; it does not schedule a separate wildlife-watching activity.

The practical question is how much time to allow between flights, border crossings and entering the two parts of the park. Heavy rain and changes in water levels sometimes affect access to particular walkways. We coordinate the sequence of visits according to actual conditions, while park opening arrangements must be confirmed before departure.

## When to add Patagonia

Another landscape-focused alternative is the [17-day itinerary through Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Uruguay](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/). It has a different structure. First come Chile's [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) and Argentina's [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) with [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). Buenos Aires, Uruguay, Iguazu and Rio follow.

Patagonia offers a very different kind of natural experience: glaciers, mountain lakes, steppes and protected areas. Guanacos, Andean condors and other species inhabit Torres del Paine, but sightings depend on the itinerary, weather and animal behaviour. The tour includes a park visit; specialist photography or dedicated wildlife tracking cannot automatically be treated as included.

Pack clothing **for two climates**: cool, windy Patagonia and the humid Iguazu region. A glacier day and a waterfall day call for different footwear and rain protection. Transfers between Patagonia, capital cities and the tropical north also take up time that cannot be used for full days in nature.

## What Uruguay actually contributes to the nature itinerary

In [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/), the programs offer waterfront walks, city activities and beaches. This makes a pleasant continuation after Iguazu or Patagonia, but **the Uruguay stage of the selected tours generally does not include a dedicated safari, whale-watching outing or specialist birdwatching excursion**.

The 13-day tour visits Montevideo and provides several days in Punta del Este. The 17-day tour and some of the longer programs allocate far less time to Uruguay. Compare actual overnight stays, not just the appearance of the country name.

If wildlife is your priority, decide whether you want to spend several days at the beach or devote that time to national parks instead. For travellers whose interest in Uruguay is primarily cultural, the [country's culture and history tour selection](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/uruguay/) is more relevant.

## Longer journeys: nature experiences beyond the selected trio

The [20-day tour of six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) offers natural landscapes without a separate wildlife-observation program. The [32-day tour of eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) features wildlife watching on the Galápagos Islands. Both cover Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, but much of their natural content occurs outside those three countries. These longer routes also include Bolivian lagoons, while the 32-day program has dedicated days in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands.

**Do not transfer a promise of birdwatching on the Galápagos or at Bolivia's lagoons to the Uruguayan or Brazilian stage.** These are different countries and different days. For a specific habitat, you can also compare [Argentine wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/) and [Brazilian wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/) before deciding which sections to combine.

We help coordinate flights, overland journeys, overnight stays near parks and weather contingencies. The actual set of excursions, nature walks and optional activities depends on the chosen program.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay

### Can I visit both sides of Iguazu Falls on one trip?

Yes. On the 13-day tour, the Brazilian and Argentine sides are visited on consecutive days. The parks have separate entrances, and the journey involves crossing an international border.

### Do these tours guarantee sightings of wild animals?

No. A national park visit is not a guarantee of seeing any particular species. For dedicated birdwatching or tracking, examine the actual nature excursion on each day.

### Is Uruguay worth adding primarily for wildlife?

On the described itineraries, Uruguay mainly offers cities, the coast and relaxation. If observing animals is your main aim, look particularly at the Galápagos days in Ecuador on the 32-day program. Iguazu focuses on waterfalls; the Bird Park and Macuco Safari are optional, and the latter is a boat excursion to the falls, not a dedicated wildlife search.

### Should I choose 13 or 17 days?

Both programs focus on natural landscapes without a separate wildlife-watching activity. The 13-day itinerary centres on Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Uruguay. The 17-day option adds Patagonia, a glacier and Torres del Paine, together with more flights, transfers and changes of climate.

lead: >-
  Argentina and Chile are natural partners for travellers who want to see Patagonia on both sides of the Andes: Perito Moreno Glacier, lakes, mountain routes in Torres del Paine and southern cities. Another journey through the same two countries travels from Buenos Aires to wine-producing Mendoza and Santiago. The choice depends on the season, walking difficulty, conditions at mountain border crossings and number of transfers. Ada Tours helps compare existing programs and plan a realistic order of visits.
---

## Argentina and Chile: Patagonia's glaciers or Andean wine valleys?

**There are two fundamentally different ways to combine Argentina and Chile.** The first travels south through [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), national parks and Chilean Patagonia. The second connects [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) and [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), focusing on cities, wineries and the Andes.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina and Chile as main countries. Some itineraries also visit Brazil, Bolivia or Antarctica. Check the individual tour for any other countries: selecting two countries does not make all the others compulsory on every trip.

Three current itineraries are particularly useful for comparison:

- [Eight-day "Patagonian Horizons"](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chile-argentina-journey/) links Buenos Aires, Perito Moreno Glacier, Puerto Natales and Santiago.
- [The 13-day "Argentina, Chile and Patagonia"](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) adds Ushuaia, El Chaltén and more days amid southern mountains and lakes.
- [The nine-day Mendoza wine tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) covers Uco Valley, Chilean wineries and the Pacific coast near Valparaíso.

| Itinerary | Why choose it |
|---|---|
| Patagonia in 8 days | Major highlights within a shorter holiday |
| Southern regions in 13 days | Ushuaia, glaciers and mountain trails |
| Mendoza and Santiago | Wine, cities and mountain passes |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_prostory_patagonii_chili_i_argentina_v_odnom_puteshestvii,tour_source_argentina_chili_i_prekrasnaya_patagoniya,tour_source_vinnyj_tur_v_argentinu_i_chili}}

## Southern Patagonia: two countries, one mountain range

On the Argentine side, journeys often start in [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). From here, travellers visit [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in Los Glaciares National Park. For some, a walk along the viewing platforms is sufficient; others choose separate boat or ice activities if these are explicitly included and permitted under current regulations.

If [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) is on the itinerary, the focus changes. Travellers come for mountain views and trails toward Fitz Roy. A hiking day to Laguna de los Tres cannot be compared in physical difficulty with walking along Perito Moreno's viewing decks. Check duration, elevation gain, the forecast and your own fitness before choosing.

The route can then continue into Chile's [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) region. This is a major nature experience of its own: granite towers, lakes and scenic trails. **Visiting the park and completing the multi-day W Trek are different travel products.** A sightseeing tour may involve road trips, lake viewpoints and short walks; demanding hikes require suitable days, fitness and sometimes accommodation booked ahead.

Our 13-day program also includes [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) and Tierra del Fuego. The result is a much broader southern journey, but also more domestic flights. Compare the actual nights spent near nature attractions rather than just a list of names.

## The Argentina–Chile border in Patagonia

**A common planning mistake is treating the road crossing between El Calafate and Puerto Natales as a short transfer.** Road distance, two immigration services, possible queues and the weather all matter. Travel time depends on the actual route and day, making a rigid arrival time without a buffer unreliable.

Chile has separate agricultural controls for arriving travellers. The SAG service requires declaration of plant and animal products carried across the border, including items in personal baggage. **Do not leave fruit, meat products and other food purchases from Argentina in your backpack out of habit.** Pack with the rules in mind and declare items if unsure. Inspectors decide what may be brought in.

A paper or digital record of immigration entry into Chile is also important. The national immigration service uses the Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM) to document the authorised stay. On itineraries with several border crossings, check entry and exit records and retain required documents until the journey ends.

We help coordinate transfers, explain border formalities and avoid scheduling a long road journey immediately before a critical international flight. When weather affects access to a park, discuss alternative allocations of days in advance.

## Mendoza to Santiago: another route through the Andes

The [Argentina and Chile wine itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) offers both countries without a long detour to Patagonian glaciers. In Argentina, it visits [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) and [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/); in Chile, [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and the [Valparaíso–Viña del Mar coast](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/).

Mendoza and Santiago appear close in a straight line on a map, but the high Andes lie between them. The overland journey across Los Libertadores Pass depends on road conditions. Snow, ice, wind and traffic restrictions can close the crossing or delay vehicles, particularly in colder months. Do not schedule an Andean overland crossing tightly before an international flight. Even on an open road, immigration controls and driving across the pass can take longer than expected. If a program uses a flight instead, assess airport connections rather than the road crossing.

For a short holiday, the wine route is generally more coherent than trying to combine Buenos Aires, Ushuaia, Torres del Paine and Santiago. It allows time for tours and tastings without an excessive number of flights. Those interested in nature and animals can explore [wildlife trips](/interests/wildlife/); for wine, see the [food and wine section](/interests/food-and-wine/).

## When to travel: Patagonia and wine regions have different seasons

For open landscapes and many hiking routes in Patagonia, travellers often choose **late spring, summer and early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere**. From November through March, days are generally longer and tourist services more active. But wind, cold rain and even mountain snow remain possible in summer.

Trail status must be checked before a visit. For example, Chile's CONAF introduced seasonal restrictions in 2026 and changed guiding requirements in Torres del Paine depending on snow and trail conditions. This shows why the list of open trails should not be fixed for years in a booking description. On the Argentine side, the Los Glaciares park administration also recommends checking roads and trail conditions before departure.

[Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) and Santiago have different seasonal priorities. Warmer months suit winery visits, though heat can make city excursions less comfortable. In winter, snow and mountain-pass conditions matter; weather in the cities themselves is much milder than on the high roads.

For Patagonia, pack waterproof and windproof clothing, multiple warm layers, comfortable hiking boots and sun protection. The urban wine route requires lighter clothing, although mountain excursions also call for warm layers. Exact packing depends on the month, activity level and baggage allowance on domestic flights.

## Visas and documents for the two countries

For Russian citizens holding a valid international passport and travelling for tourism, **Argentina and Chile have separate visa-free travel agreements**. According to official Russian Foreign Ministry materials, both permit stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period. These are two independent regimes, not a shared visa or combined day count. Different rules may apply to other nationalities.

Chile's short-stay regime, Permanencia Transitoria, normally provides authorisation for up to 90 days; the actual permitted stay is recorded in the immigration document. Before crossing, check passport validity, entry eligibility, financial requirements and documents for the particular traveller. If the itinerary involves a flight through a third country, its transit rules must be checked separately.

Argentina also has requirements concerning medical coverage for incoming foreign tourists. Insurance for Patagonia should reflect the planned activities: walking on designated platforms and undertaking a long mountain trek carry different risks and policy terms. Do not assume that a standard travel policy covers every ascent, remote journey or possible evacuation.

As part of planning, we help review the sequence of countries, borders and transit, check documents based on participants' nationality and identify conditions that require confirmation with carriers and insurers.

## Pesos, bank cards and spending budgets

Argentina uses the **Argentine peso (ARS)** and Chile the **Chilean peso (CLP)**. Despite sharing the name "peso", these are different currencies with different exchange rates. Compare tour prices quoted in US dollars with the terms for services paid locally; do not apply Argentine currency arrangements to Chile automatically.

Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks do not operate overseas through these payment systems. With foreign-issued cards, verify permitted countries, limits and fees in advance, and prepare cash reserves according to available exchange options. US dollars may be convenient for exchange, but everyday expenses are generally easier in local currency. A particular ATM or terminal cannot be guaranteed to work.

For longer journeys involving major transfers, discuss exactly which breakfasts, transfers, park tickets, excursions and internal flights are included in **the specific** program. Calling a tour "VIP" does not prove particular inclusions. For example, the [10-day "Luxury Patagonia"](/multi-country/tour/luxury-patagonia-10-days/) has its own format and accommodation terms, which must be checked on that tour's page.

## Choosing a pace and reducing travel risks

Start with your most important experience. If you dream of Perito Moreno and Torres del Paine, allow sufficient time between [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and [Puerto Natales](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), including the road journey. If you want demanding treks, add days in the mountains rather than another capital. If you prefer wineries and two cities, choose Mendoza and Santiago.

We help compare the day-by-day program with the season, activity level and real transfer times. We discuss transportation, accommodation and guides for the selected tour, allow sensible connections and highlight places where weather can affect plans. A calmer pace can be considered for a private itinerary, but specific changes and their costs depend on the final agreed program.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I visit Argentine and Chilean Patagonia without long trekking routes?

Yes. Some programs include scenic drives and glacier viewpoints. Walking distances vary, though: visiting Perito Moreno and hiking to Laguna de los Tres require different preparation. Choose by the itinerary's days, not just park names.

### How many days do I need for Argentina and Chile?

The [eight-day Patagonia route](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chile-argentina-journey/) provides a short introduction to both sides. For Ushuaia, El Chaltén and extra walks, the [13-day option](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) is more suitable. Compare the Mendoza–Santiago wine itinerary separately, as its logistics and physical demands differ.

### Can a border crossing disrupt an excursion?

Yes, if weather, border opening arrangements or queues change the travel time. Mountain crossings are especially vulnerable. Allow a buffer and check road conditions before departure.

### What must be declared when entering Chile from Argentina?

Under SAG requirements, plant and animal products in personal luggage must be declared. If unsure whether an item is permitted, declare it and follow inspectors' instructions. Failing to declare can result in a fine.

### Does a Russian citizen need a visa for either country?

Separate visa-free tourism agreements apply to Argentina and Chile. Days of stay are counted for each country independently. Before travelling, also check transit arrangements and current document requirements for every participant.

lead: >-
  Adventures in Argentina and Chile can include hikes in Patagonia, kayaking around El Chaltén, Perito Moreno Glacier, Torres del Paine and the Atacama Desert. These experiences are not all included in every program: some tours cover several countries and devote only selected days to adventure. Here is how to choose a realistic activity level, cross-border route and season.
---

## Argentina and Chile: where the adventures begin

Among the many ways to explore [Argentina](/argentina/) and [Chile](/chile/), Patagonia is particularly appealing. On one side of the Andes lie [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) and [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). On the other side, [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), glacial lakes and Chile's mountain valleys await. Some itineraries also head much farther north to Mendoza, Santiago and Atacama, where adventure takes a very different form.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina and Chile as main countries and an "Adventure" theme. Some are dedicated active programs; others are extended sightseeing journeys where trekking, kayaking or high-altitude excursions occupy only a few days. **Choose according to the actual activities**, not just a thematic category or number of countries.

## Patagonia: glaciers, trails and water

**The Argentine side.** From [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), travellers visit [Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). Boardwalk viewpoints and boat trips offer different views of the glacier, but neither is a demanding ice trek. Such a trek requires a separate program with guides and safety rules. Check which way of visiting the glacier is included before comparing activity levels.

Around [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/), more active experiences are possible. Our excursion selection includes [kayaking in El Chaltén](/argentina/el-chalten/el-chalten-kayaking/). This activity appears among the excursion modules of the [26-day journey through Argentina and neighbouring countries](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/). Its status as a compulsory or optional activity, as well as terms and permitted physical demands, needs checking separately.

**The Chilean side.** [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) offers granite towers, lakes and waterfalls. On one itinerary, this is a major sightseeing day by car with scenic stops; another may provide longer hiking sections. The W and O circuits are separate multi-day trekking routes, and a park visit does not mean these routes are included.

Weather is especially important in Patagonia. Wind, precipitation and visibility can rapidly affect boat trips, long walks and road travel. Allowing some contingency and a realistic order of stops is better than packing several extremely demanding days together.

## From wine valleys to the desert: adventure without strenuous trekking

Active travel is also possible north of Patagonia. On the [12-day "Program for Active Travellers"](/multi-country/tour/active-adventure-tour/), the itinerary goes from Buenos Aires to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and includes a day of wine tasting and trekking in a wine valley or mountains near the city. It then heads to Torres del Paine. This is an unusual combination of an active walk in central Chile and a large nature park farther south.

Distinguish **scheduled trekking** from an option to choose one of several alternatives on a particular day. If a client needs a certain distance or difficulty level, that must be specified when agreeing the itinerary, not assumed from the title "Active."

Other tours feature the [Atacama Desert](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Walks in Moon Valley, trips to lagoons and stargazing differ markedly from Patagonian hikes: less rain, drier air and different altitude constraints. The [17-day private tour through Chile, Argentina and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) includes Atacama and Torres del Paine, followed by Perito Moreno and Mendoza in Argentina. It provides diverse natural regions without promising a multi-day hike in each.

## Which existing tours should you compare?

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_programma_dlya_aktivnykh_lyudej,tour_chile_argentina_private_grand_tour_17_days,tour_source_vsya_argentina}}

The [12-day "Program for Active Travellers"](/multi-country/tour/active-adventure-tour/) features a specific walking day near Santiago followed by a visit to Chilean Patagonia. It suits travellers seeking a mix of cities and nature. The precise structure of the walking day should be defined before booking.

The [private 17-day itinerary through Chile, Argentina and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) travels from Santiago and Easter Island to Atacama, Torres del Paine, El Calafate and Perito Moreno, then via Mendoza to Iguazu and Buenos Aires. It involves many flights and excursion stages, with Brazil as a third main country.

The [26-day Argentina and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) explores much of Argentina and also neighbouring destinations, including Chile. Compare time in El Chaltén, the kayaking arrangements and days in nature parks against the city program. A longer tour does not necessarily involve a prolonged sporting trek.

There are also extensive routes through five or more South American countries with adventure themes. On some of these, the most strenuous stages occur on Bolivia's Altiplano, while Argentina and Chile mainly feature sightseeing excursions. They are substantial journeys, but choosing one for a particular Patagonia trek without checking the individual days would be a mistake.

## Routes across the Andes: borders and transportation

Argentina and Chile are divided by the Andes, and crossing conditions vary by region. Between [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) and Santiago, travellers can cross a high mountain pass, while journeys between El Calafate and Puerto Natales in Patagonia require time for the road and border formalities. Mountain weather and crossings can affect the sequence of the entire program.

Compare overnight stays and transfers as well as distances on the map. A day at Perito Moreno and the subsequent journey to Torres del Paine can fall on different transportation days. Visiting several countries does not guarantee short connections between neighbouring parks even when they look close on a map.

Chile requires travellers to declare plant and animal products when entering, including at land borders. Documents must be verified against each traveller's citizenship and the tour's actual geographical coverage. Tours also visiting Brazil, Uruguay or Bolivia bring additional national requirements.

## Physical demands and safety

For comparing active programs, establish four parameters in advance: **walking duration, elevation gain, terrain and whether specialist guidance is required**. One day might involve short scenic stops, another several hours of independent trekking. Kayaking differs from walking on a maintained trail in weather, equipment and skill requirements.

Official park trails have restrictions, and dangerous weather can lead to closures. A challenging ascent or longer trek must be arranged separately, including feasibility, guide, route, overnight stays and appropriate insurance. A standard Patagonia sightseeing program generally does not include these services automatically.

Atacama and high passes also present altitude-related risks. Rapid ascent can cause altitude sickness regardless of fitness. Plan overnight stays and acclimatisation accordingly, and discuss any individual medical contraindications with a doctor.

## Season and clothing: two sides of the same journey

In southern Patagonia, the season affects daylight hours, temperatures and the likelihood of strong winds. For walking in mountain parks, the actual conditions on the excursion date matter at least as much as average climate statistics. Central Chile and Atacama have very different temperatures and weather risks. Even one tour therefore requires clothes for different areas: wind and rain protection, warm layers, suitable hiking footwear and sun protection.

If your main aim is a particular hike in Torres del Paine or a water-based activity in Argentina, first check its seasonal availability and then arrange cities and other countries around it. We help design a trip around the priority experience rather than assemble a list of attractions without time to visit them.

## Frequently asked questions about active tours in Argentina and Chile

### Does every adventure tour include trekking in Torres del Paine?

No. Some programs visit by car with walks to viewpoints. Multi-day trekking must appear in the actual day-by-day schedule or be agreed separately.

### Can I combine kayaking in Argentina with glaciers in Chile?

Possibly, depending on dates and itinerary. The catalogue includes [El Chaltén kayaking](/argentina/el-chalten/el-chalten-kayaking/) and tours of southern Chile. Combining them, arranging transportation and confirming water conditions requires a specific program.

### Are there short programs covering only Argentina and Chile?

Yes. The selection includes a [12-day active itinerary](/multi-country/tour/active-adventure-tour/), though always check the complete list of main countries on the tour page. Other options also visit Brazil or pass through Bolivia.

### Do I need specialist equipment for Perito Moreno?

Ordinary walks on equipped viewing platforms have different requirements from ice outings. Specialist glacier routes require separate organised guidance. Do not assume an ice trek is included simply because Perito Moreno appears in a tour title.

### How should I choose between Atacama and Patagonia?

Atacama features arid high-altitude desert landscapes and lagoon excursions; Patagonia offers glaciers, lakes and mountain parks. For extended hiking, check the actual program, not just the region. Compare options in [all multi-country adventure trips](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

  On a journey through Argentina and Chile, the beach experience centres on Anakena on Easter Island. White sand and the ocean stand alongside ancient stone moai, before the route continues to Atacama, Patagonia, Mendoza and Buenos Aires. Find out how much time is actually spent by the sea, why this is different from a conventional beach holiday and how to choose the season and flights.

## Where to find the beach on a journey through Argentina and Chile

[Chile](/chile/) has an extremely long coastline, but the beach stop on this itinerary is not on its mainland coast. It is scheduled on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), or Rapa Nui, in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. On [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/), sand, palm trees and the ocean share a setting with the ancient Ahu Nau Nau archaeological complex.

In [Argentina](/argentina/), the chosen route visits different natural and cultural regions: [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), Perito Moreno Glacier, Mendoza wineries and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). **The program does not provide an extended beach stay in Argentina.** The "Argentina + Chile / Beach Holidays" combination should therefore be understood as an extensive journey with an ocean beach visit during its Chilean stage.

Our thematic selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The principal program is the [17-day private grand tour of Chile, Argentina and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/). Brazil is a third main country because the route visits both sides of Iguazu Falls. The entire journey includes all three countries, even though the focus here is Argentina and Chile.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_chile_argentina_private_grand_tour_17_days}}

## Anakena and Rapa Nui: a beach between visits to moai

Several consecutive days of the program take place on Easter Island. After flying from Santiago, travellers see Rano Kau Volcano and the ceremonial village of Orongo before following the coast to ancient ahu and stone quarries. The day at [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) also includes Ahu Akahanga, Rano Raraku, Ahu Tongariki and other archaeological sites.

This makes the stop unusual: you can explore Rapa Nui history and its moai statues in one part of the day, then reach a sandy ocean shore in another. But **a beach visit within an excursion program does not mean a full free day for swimming**. Time at Anakena must fit the excursion schedule, national park access rules, transfers and weather.

The itinerary provides two overnight stays on the island. After visiting Ahu Akivi, the Puna Pau quarry and Tahai, the group flies back to the mainland. Spending longer on Rapa Nui would therefore require a separately costed itinerary with extra nights, not a service automatically included in this tour.

## Why the beach stage is brief: the geography of the 17-day itinerary

The journey connects several natural regions of South America, with the ocean coast as only one of them.

| Stage | Experience |
|---|---|
| Santiago and Rapa Nui | Moai history and Anakena Beach |
| Atacama | Desert valleys and volcanic landscapes |
| Chilean Patagonia | Torres del Paine and mountain lakes |
| Argentine Patagonia | Perito Moreno Glacier |
| Mendoza | Wineries and tastings |
| Iguazu and Buenos Aires | Falls, city and tango |

Easter Island involves a major geographical change. The flight between Santiago and Rapa Nui takes a substantial part of a day; the program quotes approximately 5.5 hours each way on a private charter. Then come journeys to the northern Atacama and the far southern Patagonia. These flights consume time that would otherwise be available for relaxation on a conventional beach holiday.

Part of the program uses private aviation. **Private jets are priced separately** and are not included in the base price of the 17-day land itinerary. When comparing tours, do not assume a journey combining Easter Island and several long flights will cost the same as a standard mainland city tour.

## Weather on Easter Island and choosing travel dates

Anakena lies in a subtropical oceanic climate, unlike both arid Atacama and cool Patagonia. Even when the air is pleasantly warm, swimming conditions depend on winds, waves and current sea warnings. On a particular day, an archaeological excursion may be more comfortable than a prolonged beach stay.

Choosing dates for the entire journey requires a compromise: you want good weather at the water on Rapa Nui, comfortable excursions in Atacama and enough time among the mountains and glaciers of Patagonia. **No weather window guarantees perfect conditions in all these places at once.** Planning therefore begins with the trip's main priority: the beach, island history, Patagonia or the complete route.

Rapa Nui has its own entry conditions for visitors, in addition to the usual requirements for entering Chile. Before booking, confirm travel documents and registration, permitted duration of stay, accommodation and local national park visiting rules. Some archaeological areas may require an accredited guide. Check the current arrangements against citizenship and the exact flight dates.

## When to choose something else

If your aim is a full week by the sea, this 17-day grand tour includes too many compulsory transfers and cultural and nature excursions for that purpose. It is better viewed as a combination of [history and culture](/interests/culture-and-history/) with an ocean beach day on Easter Island. For a leisurely, extended seaside holiday, compare [Ada Tours beach programs](/interests/beach-holidays/) and see where the beach is the principal part of the journey.

If instead you want to visit [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/), see the moai and then explore Argentine Patagonia and Buenos Aires, the itinerary offers a coherent framework. Changing its sequence, adding island nights or removing distant stages requires new logistics and flight calculations. You can start with [all Argentina and Chile routes](/multi-country/argentina_chile/) and then decide which stages to retain.

## Frequently asked questions about beach holidays in Argentina and Chile

### How many full beach days are included?

There is no separate full beach day. Anakena is visited on an Easter Island excursion day that also includes archaeological sites. Any free time at the water must be arranged separately.

### Where exactly is Anakena Beach?

[Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) is on Easter Island, Chile, far from the country's mainland. The itinerary includes a flight from Santiago to the island and back.

### Is there a beach stage in Argentina?

This specific tour does not include an extended beach holiday in Argentina. Its Argentine section focuses on Patagonia, Mendoza, the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires.

### Can I add more nights on Easter Island?

That would require a custom change to the itinerary, including accommodation, flight dates and subsequent transfers. Extra island nights are not included in this grand tour.

### Is private aviation included in the base price?

No. Private jets and certain flight segments are charged separately. The flights included and their costs are calculated for the chosen dates and itinerary.

## Cruises in Argentina and Chile: what connects the different routes?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. All cover Chile and Argentina, but their purposes differ: a short expedition through Tierra del Fuego's fjords, a longer voyage along Chilean Patagonia, an extensive land-and-sea journey, and a trip adding Antarctica to these countries.

The first question is **where the sea journey begins and where the vessel arrives**. [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/), Puerto Montt and [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) are in very different parts of a vast southern region. Two tours both described as "Patagonian fjords" may sail through entirely different waters and last different lengths of time.

The format of shore excursions is equally important. During expedition cruises, small boats take travellers to natural areas where conditions allow landings. Wind, swell, ice and the captain's decisions can alter the sequence and even prevent an individual landing. **Cape Horn on an itinerary does not guarantee stepping ashore at Cape Horn.**

## Five days: Tierra del Fuego's fjords from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia

The ["Tierra del Fuego Fjords" cruise](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/) lasts **five days**, sailing from Punta Arenas in Chile to Ushuaia in Argentina. It suits travellers who want to concentrate on the southern straits and glaciers and leave other experiences in Argentina or Chile for a separate stage.

After boarding in [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/), the ship crosses the Strait of Magellan and heads for [Ainsworth Bay](/chile/place/ainsworth-bay/) and the Tucker Islets. Next are [Pía Glacier](/chile/place/pia-glacier/) and Glacier Alley, historic [Wulaia Bay](/chile/place/wulaia-bay/) and [Cape Horn](/chile/place/cape-horn/). The journey ends with disembarkation in Ushuaia.

Shore excursions involve inflatable boats and walking. Full board, an open bar and entertainment are listed on board. However, landing at a particular glacier or on Cape Horn depends on conditions that day. Cruise operator Australis explicitly states that landing on Cape Horn depends on the weather. That uncertainty is part of an expedition and should be considered when planning.

[Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) marks the end of the sea section. Travellers can then explore Tierra del Fuego National Park or continue to other parts of Argentina, if those days form part of the selected tour.

## Nine days: Chilean fjords from Puerto Montt

["Patagonia and Chilean Fjords"](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chilean-fjords/) is a **nine-day** expedition route. Unlike the shorter Tierra del Fuego cruise, it begins much farther north at **Puerto Montt** and sails south along Chile's coast through a network of bays, fjords and channels.

The itinerary names the areas of San Rafael and Bernardo O'Higgins national parks, Messier Channel, the Strait of Magellan, Tierra del Fuego and final arrival in Ushuaia. It covers a much longer stretch of Chilean Patagonia by sea than the five-day crossing from Punta Arenas.

These days are genuinely expeditionary: the ship travels through narrow channels among islands and glacier-covered landscapes, while landings and small-boat outings depend on weather and navigation conditions. The main attraction is extended sailing along the Pacific coast rather than visits to numerous towns. If sea landscapes and Chilean fjords are your priority, compare this route first.

Confirm the departure port of the exact cruise selected: **Puerto Montt → Ushuaia** must not be confused with **Punta Arenas → Ushuaia**. These routes begin at different ports and cover different coastal sections.

## Eighteen days: Bolivia, Patagonia and a cruise between Chile and Argentina

The [18-day "Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Patagonia" tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/) combines a long overland journey with a separate sea section. Its opening days explore Santiago, the Atacama Desert, high-altitude lagoons and Bolivia's Uyuni salt flat. Travellers then return to Chile, head to Puerto Natales and visit Torres del Paine.

**The cruise begins on day seven, not day one**, following a transfer from Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas. The sea route includes Ainsworth Bay, the Tucker Islets, Pía Glacier, Glacier Alley, Wulaia Bay and Cape Horn. The vessel arrives in Ushuaia, where the journey continues through Argentina, including Buenos Aires and Bariloche with lakes, mountains and separate catamaran excursions.

This is an attractive choice for travellers who want an expedition cruise, high-altitude Bolivia and several Argentine regions. But time aboard is only part of the 18 days. If the fjords and glaciers matter most, compare the actual **duration of the sea section** with the separate five-day cruise.

The program also includes a New Year's Eve celebration in Buenos Aires. This combination may appeal to those wanting a multi-country journey with dramatically changing natural environments, although festive arrangements and departure dates must be confirmed for the chosen trip.

## Six days: Antarctica via Cape Horn, returning by air

On the [six-day "Antarctica and Patagonia Express" tour](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/), Chile and Argentina are part of a broader geographical itinerary, with **Antarctica as the third destination**. The sea journey begins in Ushuaia, passes through the Beagle Channel and Cape Horn, and then crosses Drake Passage toward the South Shetland Islands.

The program ends at King George Island. After the Antarctic stage, travellers **fly to Punta Arenas** rather than sailing back across Drake Passage on the same vessel. The cruise-and-flight combination changes the format of the return journey. Crucially, *the outward sea crossing of Drake Passage remains part of this itinerary*.

Choose this trip for an Antarctic expedition and the southern seascapes. It differs from both classic Chilean fjord cruises and the short Punta Arenas–Ushuaia crossing. Sea conditions, shore landings and the order of expedition activities depend on safety, navigation and rules governing visits to Antarctica.

The International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators, IAATO, requires visitor briefings and has separate regulations for shore landings and vessel-only nature observation. Discuss landing details for the actual sailing rather than relying on the broad word "cruise" in a title.

## Four itineraries: durations and ports

| Program | Duration | Voyage and main countries |
|---|---:|---|
| [Tierra del Fuego Fjords](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/) | 5 days | Punta Arenas → Cape Horn → Ushuaia; Chile and Argentina |
| [Patagonia and Chilean Fjords](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chilean-fjords/) | 9 days | Puerto Montt → Chilean channels and fjords → Ushuaia |
| [Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/) | 18 days | Punta Arenas → Ushuaia sea section within a longer trip |
| [Antarctica and Patagonia Express](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/) | 6 days | Ushuaia → Antarctica, return flight to Punta Arenas |

These four programs cannot be compared solely by their number of days. Much of the 18-day tour is overland, while nearly all of the nine-day voyage centres on expedition sailing. The six-day option explores another region: Antarctic waters rather than Chilean Patagonia alone.

The [Argentina and Chile selection](/multi-country/argentina_chile/) shows the full geographical scope. Other expeditions with different combinations are available in the [multi-country cruise catalogue](/multi-country/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/).

## Glaciers, animals and shore landings: realistic expectations

Southern fjords are valued for glaciers, coastal forests, islands and seabirds seen from the ship. In clear weather, a Punta Arenas–Ushuaia voyage offers views of Tierra del Fuego's mountains, glacial fronts and narrow passages between islands. Some sailings pass near colonies of penguins and other seabirds, but wildlife inhabiting the region does not guarantee sightings of specific species on a particular voyage.

Shore visits differ from standard land-based sightseeing tours. Even when Cape Horn is on the route, **landing is possible only in suitable conditions**. An operator may arrange another landing or limit the experience to observation from aboard. The distance from which glaciers are seen also depends on the weather and the daily route. On a Patagonian voyage, the experience of sailing through the seascape matters more than a promise of one particular photograph.

If going ashore at a certain location is essential, discuss the likelihood and rules beforehand. If you want the greatest possible time among glaciers and sheltered channels, compare the nine-day Chilean Patagonia route with the five-day Tierra del Fuego voyage.

## Preparing for a sea expedition

For a cruise through southern Patagonia, bring windproof and waterproof clothing, non-slip shoes and several warm layers. Weather can change rapidly in the southern straits even in summer. Small-boat landings depend on the crew's instructions, and participation should be considered in light of these requirements.

Leave enough time between flights and embarkation. The ship's departure port, check-in time, any overnight stay before departure and the final transfer affect the whole itinerary. This is especially important for journeys with a return flight from Antarctica and for programs in which the cruise forms the middle of a long tour.

Compare the price and inclusions of each specific sailing: cabins, meals, drinks, guided landings, domestic flights and extra land days can be included in different parts of a program. Do not apply the five-day cruise's terms to a longer land-and-sea itinerary merely because some of the voyage is shared.

## Frequently asked questions about cruises between Argentina and Chile

### Which cruise should I choose if I have only five days?

Consider ["Tierra del Fuego Fjords"](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/): a separate five-day voyage from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia, with Pía Glacier, Ainsworth Bay, Wulaia and Cape Horn on its route.

### What is the difference between cruises from Puerto Montt and Punta Arenas?

The [nine-day voyage from Puerto Montt](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chilean-fjords/) explores a longer stretch of Chile's coastline. The [five-day cruise from Punta Arenas](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/) focuses on the Strait of Magellan and Tierra del Fuego. The departure port changes the voyage's actual geography.

### Is a landing on Cape Horn guaranteed?

No. The itinerary schedules a passage past Cape Horn and a possible landing. Wind, swell and safety determine whether it can happen, as expedition cruise operators explicitly state.

### Can I add Antarctica and avoid Drake Passage?

On the [six-day Express air-cruise](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/), **the return sea crossing of Drake Passage is replaced by a flight**, but the outward journey from Ushuaia to Antarctica still crosses Drake Passage by sea.

### Is there a tour combining a cruise and Bolivia?

Yes. The [18-day route](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/) includes high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni before embarkation in Punta Arenas, followed by visits in Argentina.
